subject.title: Feature Request: WhatsApp sticker send support

question: Should public WhatsApp sticker sending require sticker-ready WebP media, or should OpenClaw convert supported source images into valid WhatsApp stickers?
rationale: The transport primitive and plugin ownership are established, but accepted source formats, animation support, conversion behavior, and rejection semantics are a user-facing product contract that source inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Convert supported images
options.body: Add an explicit sticker action that normalizes common static images into valid WhatsApp sticker WebP and clearly rejects unsupported animated inputs.

options.title: Prepared WebP only
options.body: Expose the action but require callers to provide sticker-ready WebP meeting documented size, dimension, animation, and metadata requirements.

options.title: Infer ordinary media sends
options.body: Automatically reinterpret qualifying captionless WebP files from the normal send path as stickers, accepting implicit behavior and weaker intent clarity.

recommendation.title: Convert supported images
recommendation.body: Add an explicit sticker action that normalizes common static images into valid WhatsApp sticker WebP and clearly rejects unsupported animated inputs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main refactor introduced both the low-level sticker sender and the adjacent action descriptor where the public contract would be completed.
